newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran oil refinery output unaffected by strike.
newsitem.headline: Iran oil refinery output unaffected by strike.

text.p: Refinery operations at the 225,000 barrel per day (bpd) Tehran oil refinery are running normally despite protests this week by plant workers, an official at the National Iranian Oil Company (NIOC) said on Wednesday.

"We had a strike but just now there is no problem. All of the workers are working now...There is no problem with the production," Sayyed Reza Kasaeizadeh, NIOC's director of refining affairs, said by telephone from Tehran.
NIOC's Tehran refinery is the main source of the transport and heating fuels for the capital's seven million people.
Police in riot gear arrested on Sunday busloads of oil workers among a thousand protestors from the refinery who had demonstrated at Iran's petroleum ministry.
Tehran refinery, the third largest in the country, was also the site of a two-week long hunger strike by workers in 1992 demanding wage increases.
Capacity of Iran's eight refineries is 1.2 million bpd.
